phenomenon_scale.label: 184 µm
phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Larval flank chromatophore primordium: melanophore–xanthophore spacing selected at the Turing onset wavenumber

chronoseries.name: Ambystoma
chronoseries.what_changes_at_this_scale: With only one chronospecies node, the contrast is across length, not across named fossil species. Below 184 µm the flank is a migrating neural-crest population (Erickson 1993) and no chemical wavelength is selected. At 0.0001843 m the Schnakenberg onset mode k_c = 2π/184.3 µm is the first unstable pigment spacing. Above this length the same Holocene pattern is stretched by domain growth (Murray 1981) into adult ocelli; that longer spacing is a later scale of this species, not a successor chronospecies, and it is not fitted here.

equations.activator: dt u = Du laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v
equations.inhibitor: dt v = Dv laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
equations.onset_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.boundary_conditions: Periodic on the square primordium patch. The circular vignette in the GIF is a display mask copied from the micrograph's field stop, not a Neumann or Dirichlet condition.

parameter_table.why_this_ratio: Just above the Turing threshold so the fastest-growing wavenumber stays near the onset wavenumber. A deeply supercritical ratio (for example 20) shifts the fastest mode to a longer wavelength and is not used.
parameter_table.not_copied_from: Ambystoma maculatum sibling slots use a different species and different parameters. This ratio, steady state, and 184.3 µm onset length are specific to loop 3107.

empirical_claims: Epperlein & Löfberg (1989) describe the larval pigment pattern of Ambystoma mexicanum as an arrangement of melanophores and other chromatophores, not as a measured 184.3 µm Turing wavelength.
Frost-Mason & Mason (1996) review axolotl pigmentation as a developmental system. They do not publish this wavenumber.
The length 0.0001843 m is the Delphi scale coordinate for tier 5_primordium_100um, detail variant. The model is built so the onset wavelength equals that coordinate.
The vendored micrograph shows melanophores and xanthophores inside a circular field. It has no scale bar, so the script does not convert its pixel spacing into micrometres.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 dispersion relation and diffusion-driven instability conditions
Murray 1981 pre-pattern account of coat markings and the domain-growth scale argument
Epperlein & Löfberg 1989 larval Ambystoma mexicanum pigment pattern
Frost-Mason & Mason 1996 review of axolotl pigmentation
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg parameters (a, b, Dv/Du) = (0.10, 0.90, 9) chosen so the onset wavelength is 184.3 µm
Spectral integration on a periodic 8-wavelength patch
Linear dispersion sweep, ablation at Dv/Du = 1, and pixel segmentation of the micrograph
transfer_boundary: No axolotl paper cited here measured 184.3 µm. Agreement of the linear fastest mode with 184.3 µm tests the algebra of this reconstruction, not a wet-lab spacing.
Zebrafish stripe RD papers are not used as the axolotl law.
Adult ocellus size is not predicted numerically in this slot.
does_not_claim: That lab axolotl color morphs (leucistic, albino, melanoid) are this wild-type wavelength
That the species-gallery limb plate is a pigment specimen
A micrometre measurement read off the Wikimedia micrograph
